title: SKYSHIELD Alert
description: Canonical semantic definition of a SKYSHIELD alert. This schema is the single source of truth for alert MEANING. The BLE wire format is a compact CBOR encoding of this same model, defined in docs/wire-protocol.md. JSON is used for documentation, fixtures, and tooling; CBOR is used on the wire. The two must always carry identical semantics.

protocol_version.description: Wire/semantic contract version. Incremented on any breaking change to field meaning or CBOR key assignment. Version 3 is the first CBOR-based version; versions 1 and 2 were the retired pipe-delimited S1/S2 formats and are not accepted.

timestamp_ms.description: Milliseconds since CORE (ESP32) boot, sampled when CORE finished normalizing the alert and immediately before BLE transmission. This is a MONOTONIC device-local clock, not wall-clock or Unix epoch: the bridge has no RTC or time sync. Consumers must not treat it as an absolute time.

detector_latency_ms.description: Optional. Milliseconds elapsed between CORE ingesting the raw detector line and CORE finishing normalization (timestamp_ms). Both endpoints are sampled from the same CORE clock, so this is an exact detector-to-CORE latency measurement with no clock-sync assumptions. Omitted when the alert did not originate from a detector line.

sequence.description: Monotonic packet counter from the bridge. Lets the watch detect duplicates and gaps.

sensor_type.description: Physical sensing modality that produced this alert. Reserved for future multi-sensor fusion; only 'rf' is produced today.

alert_kind.description: 'classified' means the detector supplied usable threat/band/strength data. 'contact' is a FIRST-CLASS data-less detection: something was detected but the detector could not classify it. A contact alert legitimately carries threat=UNKNOWN, band=UNKNOWN and confidence=null. It is a valid operational state, NOT a parse failure or error fallback.

band.description: Primary frequency band. UNKNOWN is required so a contact alert can be expressed without inventing a band.

distance.description: Legacy protocol term for coarse RF signal-strength category, NOT physical range. The Garmin HUD renders FAR as WEAK, MID as MODERATE, NEAR as STRONG. UNKNOWN is required for contact alerts.

confidence.description: Classification confidence percentage. MUST be null (not 0) when the detector supplies no confidence value, so that 'no data' is distinguishable from 'certainly not'. Contact alerts always carry null.

drone_class.description: Optional vendor/model classification from the detector, such as MAVIC, AUTEL, FPV or UNKNOWN. Supplied by the detector or middleware; the watch must never invent it.

direction.description: Optional coarse bearing hint for future directional RF workflows. Experimental; not displayed on the HUD.

bands.description: Optional per-band activity levels. Omitted entirely when the detector does not report per-band data. Consumers must render omitted band data as unknown rather than synthesizing it.

source.description: Optional source label identifying the producing adapter, such as TTSKW07, MOCK or SERIAL_INJECT.
